content.thinking: Found the likely cause: `DeleteExpiredAsync` in the EF repository deletes domains with a stale `LastCheckedDate` without checking verification status. Now checking the Dapper repository and SQL procedure for the same issue.

file.content:
CREATE PROCEDURE [dbo].[OrganizationDomain_DeleteIfExpired]
    @ExpirationPeriod TINYINT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT OFF
        
    DELETE FROM [dbo].[OrganizationDomain]
    WHERE DATEDIFF(DAY, [LastCheckedDate], GETUTCDATE()) >= @ExpirationPeriod
    AND [VerifiedDate] IS NULL
END

content.text: The SQL procedure used by Dapper already filters on `VerifiedDate IS NULL`. The EF version doesn't, which matches the Postgres setup in the report.

files.reason: DeleteExpiredAsync (EF/Postgres) deletes any domain with a stale LastCheckedDate and has no VerifiedDate == null filter, unlike the SQL Server proc. This is the likely root cause of verified domains vanishing.
OrganizationDomainMaintenanceAsync calls DeleteExpiredAsync and logs only a status. It doesn't log or emit an event for the domains it deletes, which is the missing-trace part of the report.
The SQL Server delete procedure. It already has the VerifiedDate IS NULL filter, so it is the reference for the EF fix.
The Dapper DeleteExpiredAsync calls the delete proc. Worth checking for parity with the EF repository.
Verification and LastCheckedDate handling. Verified domains are never re-checked, so LastCheckedDate goes stale.
The repository interface for DeleteExpiredAsync and GetExpiredOrganizationDomainsAsync. It would change if the delete returns the deleted domains for logging.
